races.name: Tapestry Events EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Unite John Gillespie Celebration Handicap

runners_data.name: Henery Hawk
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter who sets the race up from the front; seven-year-old veteran with two recent top-three finishes at this exact trip and a win at Stanmore in current form, though carrying 138lbs on soft ground is a stamina question in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: King Of The Jungle
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent racer whose recent win came on good ground at this trip; similar-going form shows a win and a place from 15 runs suggesting soft is not his forte, though Billy Garritty is an astute reader of pace and the Easterby yard has two winners from 35 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Keep The Gold
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer who has placed twice at this trip on good ground recently; blinkers go on for Michael Dods, the trainer has been in form (3 from 23 past 14 days), and soft going at this distance is a slight unknown, though the horse's consistency keeps it relevant.

runners_data.name: Auntie Jo
runners_data.note: Progressive filly who won her last start at Stanmore and placed on similar ground over this trip; Sam James keeps the ride, the O'Meara yard is firing (5 from 48), and she wears a hood — her prominent style suits the expected pace shape well.

runners_data.name: Wee Mary
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for Jim Goldie who won last time out on good ground at 5f and is fitted with a hood; three-pound claiming rider Amie Waugh takes 3lbs off, and while the soft going is an unknown, her recent form is strong enough to warrant respect even from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Great Profit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up runner whose sole soft-ground start produced his best finishing position (8th of a large field); the drop to 5f is a new test — the Harrison yard has been quiet (1 from 3) and 33 days off adds uncertainty, though soft ground could theoretically unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Royal Duke
runners_data.note: Modest hold-up performer whose record at this trip on comparable ground is uninspiring (10th on soft, mostly 6th-10th finishes); the R Mike Smith yard is without a recent winner (0 from 7), and with the horse mapped out of its natural position the style-fit flag tempers confidence significantly.

runners_data.name: Supremissy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who carries a fade flag based on recent finishes; the Iain Jardine yard has 2 from 17 in the fortnight and the horse has been off 48 days — mapped to midfield though a natural hold-up type who needs conditions to suit, and the evidence of fading late on soft going is a real deterrent.

runners_data.name: Regal Dream
runners_data.note: Wears blinkers and has a hold-up style that has produced only two placed efforts from 11 recent starts; the Kevin Ryan yard shows 3 from 25 recently but 61 days off the track is significant, and the horse's record on soft ground is poor — pushed into a midfield map position away from natural habitat.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Has raced five days ago (quick turnaround) and the R Mike Smith stable has been quiet; the horse's best recent finish was a second at 6f on good ground, and while it has placed on soft-equivalent surfaces, its true hold-up style is at odds with the expected race shape, making the style displacement a genuine handicap here.

runners_data.name: Bonito Cavalo
runners_data.note: Veteran seven-year-old with a consistent record of finishing in the 7th-11th range at this track; carries a fade flag, has been off 68 days, and its entire recent form on Stanmore has been poor — the true hold-up profile mapped to midfield further reduces the realistic prospect of a winning run.

races.paceDynamic: Henery Hawk is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead on soft ground over 5f, should be able to bowl along at a sustainable clip without being pressured into burning out early. King Of The Jungle and Auntie Jo are the most credible prominent racers who will look to sit just off Henery Hawk's heels, creating an orderly pace scenario rather than a contested, tactical scramble. On soft going at Ayr over 5f, a race run at steady-to-fair fractions with a single leader and two honest chasers behind typically sets up best for horses who can travel prominently and sustain their effort through the short closing stages — genuine hold-up horses rarely get enough juice in the final furlong to reel in those who have conserved energy just off the pace. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get their natural rear position; Supremissy, Regal Dream, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, and Bonito Cavalo are all true closers redistributed into midfield on the map, and of these only the freshest or most versatile will manage to find any meaningful late position, making prominent racers the clearly favoured profile here.

scenarios.title: Hawk Leads, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Henery Hawk controls the race cleanly from the front and the pace remains honest but not frantic on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: If Henery Hawk controls the race cleanly from the front and the pace remains honest but not frantic on the soft ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Saps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the soft going proves more testing than Henery Hawk can handle across the final furlong and the lead weakens late.
scenarios.body: If the soft going proves more testing than Henery Hawk can handle across the final furlong and the lead weakens late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the pace set by Henery Hawk is quicker than expected early, stringing the field out and leaving a genuine gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: If the pace set by Henery Hawk is quicker than expected early, stringing the field out and leaving a genuine gap for a late finisher.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Mover Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If a lightly-raced or unexposed horse improves markedly on the day and wins despite an unfashionable position in the pace map.
scenarios.body: If a lightly-raced or unexposed horse improves markedly on the day and wins despite an unfashionable position in the pace map.

watchPoints.text: Henery Hawk is the sole pace-setter — if she misses the break or is slow from the stalls, the race is suddenly leader-less and the entire pace dynamic changes instantly.

King Of The Jungle and Auntie Jo are both prominent types likely to contest the same ground just off the leader; a scrimmage for position in the early stages on soft going could compromise both horses' chances and open the door for a fresher rival.

Wee Mary and Keep The Gold are the two most credible hold-up performers in this field based on current form — monitor whether the pace is genuinely strong enough to draw them into contention late, as the soft going may not generate sufficient early fractions.

Five runners (Supremissy, Regal Dream, Royal Duke, Ski Angel, Bonito Cavalo) are redistributed from their true hold-up position — watch for traffic issues and interference in the final two furlongs if several of these try to find gaps simultaneously from midfield.
Great Profit represents the only lightly-exposed angle at 5f on soft — worth watching in-running to see if the trip and conditions unlock any improvement that bare form figures do not suggest.

races.name: Unite Natalie Egan Celebration Handicap (For The Johnstone Rose Bowl) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Albany
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who maps neatly onto lead but carries a STYLE_FIT flag — she has been racing prominently rather than making the running and her form figures (6/026-) include modest efforts in better company; Hector Crouch takes over for Ralph Beckett after a 289-day absence and fitness must be taken on trust.

runners_data.name: Square Necker
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart De Foy has a strong recent strike rate (1/17 in 14 days) and Square Necker's form reading — 31-21 — shows he finishes races off, with a win on soft in his recent history; Sam James is an astute partner at this level and the 1m3f-1m4f form suggests this step to 1m5f on soft is a genuine stamina test to pass.

runners_data.name: Dancingwithmyself
runners_data.note: Has won three times on soft or softer going and the form string (1-2-3 over 1m4f-1m6f on soft) is directly relevant to today's conditions; Oisin Orr keeps the ride for Michael Bell, whose in-form stable (1/19 in 14 days) adds confidence, and this trip-going combination is where this horse has repeatedly delivered.

runners_data.name: Oneforthegutter
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator but his recent form string (0008-7) shows little sign of life, with a string of poor finishings over various trips and surfaces; Paul Mulrennan takes over but the soft-ground placed record (0W1P from 3 runs) is thin and this seven-year-old looks hard to trust at present.

runners_data.name: Peaky Blinder
runners_data.note: Won over 1m6f on soft and 1m4f on soft recently (1-1 in sim-going), so conditions are firmly in his favour; Jason Hart rides for Andrew Balding whose 14-day strike rate (9/63) shows strong team form, and the headgear (hg:p) suggests a horse that needs to be anchored in a race — likely to track Albany closely.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is naturally a front-running type but the crowded prominent positions in this field mean he is unlikely to get that forward berth — his best form has come when stalking the pace, so he may adapt better than the redistribution flag implies; the soft-going record is limited (1W1P from 7 runs) and the step up from 1m2f to 1m5f is the central query.

runners_data.name: Boatswain
runners_data.note: The Simon & Ed Crisford runner has headgear noted (hg:p) and was last seen only 24 days ago — freshness is not an issue; a true front-running type squeezed into midfield by the numbers, his soft-going record from nine runs is modest (0W0P) and the distance jump from 1m4f to 1m5f in testing conditions raises a stamina question.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Has raced exclusively on good or faster ground (sim-going: 1W1P from 12 runs all on good), making today's soft surface a significant and largely unanswered question; Mikey Sheehy takes the ride with a visor (hg:v) and Charlie Johnston's team is in solid 14-day form (4/34), but the going query is the dominant factor here.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: William Haggas has been firing (11/53 in 14 days) and Harry Davies is an able deputy, but Divine Knight has raced almost exclusively at shorter distances — 1m to 1m2f — and is another genuine prominent type pushed into a midfield slot by the pace map; the trip extension to 1m5f on soft is a serious unknown for this horse's profile.

runners_data.name: Letsbefrank
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has been in fine form recently (75-113), winning twice over 1m2f-1m4f on good ground, and Lauren Young (claim 5lb) reduces the weight; the soft-going record (0W0P from 3 runs at this level) is not strong, but the horse is racing into form and the trip should suit a hold-up style if the race develops into a true test.

runners_data.name: Humble Spark
runners_data.note: A consistent placer (442262) whose last five runs all came on good or good-to-firm ground — the step to soft is a concern given no win or place on similar going from 15 attempts; Amie Waugh claims 3lb for the same Goldie yard, and the horse ran just seven days ago, meaning residual fatigue on soft ground could be a factor in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Ran well to win over 1m6f on good ground (1/18f/GOO) but her recent figures (012-00) suggest she has gone off the boil, and Warren Fentiman's claim (3lb) is unlikely to compensate for the trainer's modest strike rate (0/8 in 14 days); the soft-going form from nine runs shows one placed effort without a win, and this is a notable query for her in these conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Albany is the one confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead likely to press hard from the outset, she should be able to dictate at a sustainable clip over 1m5f on soft ground at Ayr. That controlled, unexploited lead creates a race that will likely be run at a measured early tempo, compressing the field into a bunched formation through the middle stages before the real race ignites in the straight. On soft turf at this distance with a single pace-setter in control, hold-up horses and strong-staying prominents who can track and pounce off the bend are structurally favoured — stamina and the ability to travel comfortably through a muddling gallop matter more than raw speed. Boatswain, Ashnak, and Divine Knight are all genuine front-running or prominent types who have been displaced into midfield by the crowded nature of the pace map — in practice, Albany is the only horse likely to get a true lead, with those three likely to be frustrated slightly further back than ideal.

scenarios.title: Albany Controls, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Albany dictates a sustainable, uncontested lead and the field settles into a compressed convoy behind her.
scenarios.body: If Albany dictates a sustainable, uncontested lead and the field settles into a compressed convoy behind her.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Quicken
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the displaced prominent horses manage to land a handy position just behind Albany and kick off the home turn.
scenarios.body: If one or two of the displaced prominent horses manage to land a handy position just behind Albany and kick off the home turn.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Albany is pressured early or the pace is stronger than expected, stringing out the field and setting up a true slog.
scenarios.body: If Albany is pressured early or the pace is stronger than expected, stringing out the field and setting up a true slog.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Market Movers Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is artificially slow and a prominent horse is able to kick decisively turning for home, leaving the field flat-footed.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is artificially slow and a prominent horse is able to kick decisively turning for home, leaving the field flat-footed.

watchPoints.text: Albany's jumping-off point after 289 days off is critical — if she shows any sign of blowing up or losing her rhythm in the straight, the race opens up immediately for the hold-up horses behind her.

Boatswain, Ashnak, and Divine Knight are all prominent types likely to be denied their natural position — watch for early jostling in the first furlong as those three riders compete for handy spots behind Albany, which could inject unexpected early pace.

Pole Star has no proven soft-ground form and the visor is unlikely to unlock that — if conditions have deteriorated further by post-time, his chances narrow sharply and the market should be read with that caveat in mind.

Letsbefrank has won twice in recent weeks and Jim Goldie has seven winners from 47 runners in 14 days — watch whether Lauren Young's 5lb claim and the stable's momentum translate onto soft ground at a distance slightly beyond the horse's winning range.

Square Necker's trainer Kevin Philippart De Foy landed a winner from 17 runners in the past 14 days and the horse's sole soft-going run produced a placed effort — if he travels smoothly in behind Albany, Sam James is the type to produce him late and make the most of the pace scenario.
